name: Robotics and Autonomy
guide:
Robotics and Autonomy roles on theworldofai.org center on building the software and control systems that let a physical machine sense its environment and act inside it, rather than building a model that only classifies images or text. Titles we track include research engineer, AI scientist, and senior AI systems engineer for robotics and swarming, alongside a machine learning engineer role moving perception output into planning and control. This differs from Computer Vision work, which usually stops at extracting information from sensor data, and from Machine Learning Engineering, which usually stops at training and serving a model. A robotics and autonomy engineer takes perception and model output the rest of the way, into a control system that moves a physical or simulated body safely and repeatedly. Postings in our data reflect this blend directly, several list computer vision and reinforcement learning skills alongside C++ and distributed systems work, which is the signature combination of this discipline.

Our job data does not include a dedicated degree or certification field, so nothing on this page should be read as inventing a credential requirement. What we can say from the titles themselves is that this discipline mixes research roles, research engineer and AI scientist at Mistral.ai, with engineering roles, senior AI systems engineer at Stark, machine learning engineer at Waymo, and machine learning solutions engineer at Scale AI. No certification of any kind appears in the skills lists for any of the eleven postings we currently track in this category. That does not mean certifications never matter for a robotics role, only that none surfaced in our tracked postings. Treat degree and certification requirements as something to confirm on the individual listing rather than a fixed rule for the discipline.

Seniority in our tracked postings runs from intern to manager, with mid-level the most common tier at six of the eleven roles, followed by three senior postings and one manager-level product role. The intern listing, a robotics ML and data role at Sereact GmbH in Stuttgart, is the only entry-level opening we have recorded for this discipline. The senior postings cluster around systems and swarming work at Stark and around production robotics machine learning at Waymo, both environments where a mistake in the software has physical consequences. That pattern, senior roles concentrated where the software controls something physical, is consistent with the day to day description above. Someone building toward this discipline should expect the bar to rise sharply between mid-level model or perception work and senior roles that own how a robot behaves in the world.

The skills column across these postings names a fairly consistent toolkit. Python and C++ are the most common languages, appearing in eight and five of the eleven postings, and computer vision skills appear in seven, underscoring how tightly perception work is bundled into this discipline even though it is a distinct step from full computer vision engineering. PyTorch and reinforcement learning each appear in three postings, and GPU infrastructure appears in two, signs that a share of these roles train and iterate on control policies rather than only writing hand tuned control code. Rust appears in four postings, mostly at companies also doing broader distributed systems work, OpenAI, Waymo, Coreweaveu, and Scale AI. We saw no mention of ROS, Gazebo, or other named simulation platforms in the skills text for any of the eleven postings we track, so we are not claiming those tools are standard here, only reporting what is and is not present in our data.

As of today we currently track approximately three open postings actively live in this category, out of eleven robotics and autonomy roles we have recorded in total. Companies appearing more than once are Mistral.ai and Stark, each with two of the eleven postings, everyone else in our data, OpenAI, Physical Intelligence, Waymo, Coreweaveu, Sereact GmbH, World of VR, and Scale AI, appears once. None of the eleven postings we track carry a listed salary figure, so we cannot report a salary range for this discipline without inventing one, and we will not do that. Locations skew toward established robotics and AI hubs, San Francisco and Mountain View in the United States, and Paris, Munich, London, Cologne, and Stuttgart in Europe. This is a small, concentrated market in our data right now, and readers should treat it as a specialist niche rather than a high volume hiring category.

reading.body:
Four open roles in robotics and autonomy were tracked across leading AI companies as of September 2026, with postings from OpenAI, Waymo, Physical Intelligence, and Stark spanning distributed systems, swarming, and general robotics work.

The hiring is concentrated in established AI labs and autonomous vehicle firms rather than distributed across the sector. Three of four roles are in the United States, two explicitly in San Francisco. The jobs cluster around machine learning engineering and systems design work, suggesting that robotics capabilities depend on deep infrastructure investment rather than peripheral skill acquisition. The one European posting at Stark indicates some geographic spread, but the pattern still reflects where compute density and funding are highest.

This snapshot does not show hiring volume over time, hiring pace relative to other AI functions, or how many applications these roles receive. It captures only open positions on accessible job boards and company sites, not internal hiring or roles filled through other channels. The data says where AI robotics teams are recruiting, not how many people work in the field, how fast it is growing, or whether it is a constraint on broader AI development.
